hook.text: In 2010, Craig Venter's team built an entire bacterial genome from scratch and booted it up inside a living cell.

buildup.text: They synthesized over a million DNA base pairs, assembled them chemically, and inserted the genome into an empty cell.

discovery.text: The cell came alive, divided, and grew. It was the first organism running entirely on synthetic DNA written by humans.

twist.text: Writing whole genomes is still extremely expensive and error-prone. Each mistake can crash the cell like a software bug.

climax.text: The Genome Project-Write aims to synthesize an entire human genome. Its goal is understanding, not creating people.

punchline.text: We went from reading the code to writing it from scratch.

quiz.question: Who created the first organism running on a fully synthetic genome?
